pattern: \b(we'?re|i think we'?re|looks?|is it|are we) (all )?(done|finished|fixed|good to go|ready)\b|\b(tests?|build|ci|checks?) (now )?(pass(es|ing)?|(is|are) green)\b|\bwrite (up )?(the|a) (summary|report|release notes?)\b|\bput that in the\b|\b(says?|said|reports?|reported) (it|that|the)\b.*\b(ran|works?|passed|clean(ly)?|done)\b
say: [evidence-before-done] A claim of done, fixed, or passing needs what you observed this turn: run the real thing, read its output, then say what you ran and what it showed. Check a subagent's specific claim before repeating it. Load the evidence-before-done skill.
[evidence-before-done] "Pre-existing" is a claim to disprove: show the failure on the base commit, or treat it as yours and fix it. Load the evidence-before-done skill.

[evidence-before-done] A skipped test, a suppression, or a stub hides the problem. Fix the cause. If one has to stay, report it with the reason and do not call the work done. Load the evidence-before-done skill.

[evidence-before-done] The user ran it and it failed. Look at the failure path they describe; do not explain why it should have worked. Reproduce it before changing anything. Load the evidence-before-done skill.

[evidence-before-done] Tests do not see a screen. After a visual change, run the real build, take a screenshot, read it, and say what you saw against what was asked. If you cannot look, report the result as unseen. Load the evidence-before-done skill.
